fastrel: fast relatedness, relationship and kinship matrices from pedigrees

Source: R/fastrel-package.R
fastrel-package.Rd

Tools to compute, for autosomal loci of diploid individuals, the additive relationship ("relatedness") matrix \(A = 2\phi\) (Emik and Terrill 1949; Henderson 1976), where \(\phi\) is the kinship coefficient (Malécot 1948), as well as the kinship coefficient itself, Wright's coefficient of relationship (Wright 1922) and Hamilton's regression coefficient of relatedness (Hamilton 1972; Michod and Hamilton 1980).

Details

Two interfaces compute the relatedness matrix itself:

  • fastrel_ped() and fastrel_vec() compute the whole matrix from a pedigree in one go, given as a data frame or as vectors (the latter is a fast replacement for 2 * kinship2::kinship()).

  • rel_new(), rel_add(), rel_remove() and rel_get() maintain the matrix incrementally, which is computationally much cheaper when a pedigree keeps growing, as in an individual-based simulation. rel_ids(), rel_size() and rel_capacity() describe the content of such a store, and rel_save() and rel_load() save it to disk and restore it. rel_copy() makes an independent copy of it.

fastrel_inv() computes the inverse of the relatedness matrix (the precision matrix used by animal models) as a sparse matrix, directly from the pedigree, so that it can be obtained even for very large pedigrees.

sim_ped() simulates a pedigree, and sim_pop() a population with births, deaths, emigration and immigration, for testing and benchmarking.

The README of the package, at https://github.com/courtiol/fastrel and on the website of the package, https://courtiol.github.io/fastrel/, gives an overview with worked examples: relatedness of a whole pedigree, incremental updates in a simulation with births and deaths, metapopulations, and benchmarks against other packages.

Measures of relatedness

By default, all functions return the additive relationship \(A_{ij} = 2\phi_{ij}\), where \(\phi_{ij}\) is the kinship coefficient. The kinship coefficient is a probability: that of an allele drawn at random from \(i\) and an allele drawn at random from \(j\), at the same locus, being identical by descent. The additive relationship is instead an expected count of alleles: \(A_{ij}\) is the expected number of the two alleles of \(j\) that are identical by descent with an allele drawn at random from \(i\). This is why it lies between 0 and 2, and can exceed 1 (see relatedness_metrics). For example, an allele drawn from a parent is one of the two alleles of its offspring with probability 1/2, so their additive relationship is 0.5 without inbreeding. Its diagonal is \(1 + F_i\), where \(F_i\) is the inbreeding coefficient, so diag(A) - 1 gives the inbreeding coefficients. Founders (individuals with unknown parents) are assumed to be unrelated and non-inbred, and an unknown parent is treated as unrelated to everybody.

fastrel_ped(), fastrel_vec() and rel_get() can instead return the kinship coefficient (Malécot 1948), Wright's coefficient of relationship (Wright 1922) or Hamilton's regression coefficient of relatedness (Hamilton 1972), with their argument metric. These measures, what they mean and when to use them are described in relatedness_metrics.

The matrices are computed with the tabular method (Emik and Terrill 1949), implemented in C++. See relatedness_metrics for the full list of references.

References

Emik, L. O., & Terrill, C. E. (1949). Systematic procedures for calculating inbreeding coefficients. Journal of Heredity, 40(2), 51–55. doi:10.1093/oxfordjournals.jhered.a105986

Hamilton, W. D. (1972). Altruism and related phenomena, mainly in social insects. Annual Review of Ecology and Systematics, 3, 193–232. doi:10.1146/annurev.es.03.110172.001205

Henderson, C. R. (1976). A simple method for computing the inverse of a numerator relationship matrix used in prediction of breeding values. Biometrics, 32(1), 69–83. doi:10.2307/2529339

Malécot, G. (1948). Les mathématiques de l'hérédité. Masson et Cie, Paris.

Michod, R. E., & Hamilton, W. D. (1980). Coefficients of relatedness in sociobiology. Nature, 288, 694–697. doi:10.1038/288694a0

Wright, S. (1922). Coefficients of inbreeding and relationship. The American Naturalist, 56(645), 330–338. doi:10.1086/279872
